hero.heading: Catalyst, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built September 26, 2026, from catalystpdg.com and company posts, the Conexus Indiana case study, and federal data. Every number is labeled: published, federal, or our assumption. The assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: Exact computed endpoints: $11,137.50 and $74,355.00, rounded to the nearest $5,000 for display.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Programs you run in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per ten programs.

sliders.label: Programs that absorb one extra iteration loop
Tooling and molding value of a program
Months a fixed quote waits between signature and first articles

presets.label: We buy steel the day we quote

constants.text: Steel mill products rose 25.1 percent from September 2025 to August 2026 [[BENCHMARK]], BLS series WPU1017. This one is not a slider.

terms.label: Drift inside tooling and molding quotes

model.formulaText: Leak per 10 programs = 10 × absorbing share × loop cost + 10 × tooling value × materials share × 0.251 × (months / 12)
model.plainText: In words, the programs that absorb one extra iteration loop at its cost, plus the slice of this year's steel rise a fixed tooling and molding quote absorbs while it waits between signature and first articles.
model.callout: Client approvals gate every phase of your process. Nobody publishes the calendar days a program waits at those gates against the days your people spend working it. If the waiting belongs to clients, it is worth showing them.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: You started in 1999 with four people in five hundred square feet [[OBSERVED]].
You design, engineer, prototype, tool, and mold under one roof, on six presses, in your own words [[OBSERVED]].
Your stated reason is protecting your clients' ideas by keeping their product in one building [[OBSERVED]].
In 2022 you put a $159,500 readiness grant to work on machines [[BENCHMARK]].
